source.title: 2021 – DSE Listening – 5** Past Paper 題解書 (Edmund Sir)
source.timingBasis: PDF text matched to existing split-track transcript; navigation cues are approximate.

1.explanation: 題目問 presentation 的 Date。錄音說：“we’re presenting on August 30th at 9:30 a.m.”“presenting on August 30th” 直接對應日期，所以答案是 August 30。中伏位：後面還有 August 19、21、23、26，但那些是工作安排日期，不是正式 presentation date。

2.explanation: 題目問 presentation 的 Time。錄音說：“at 9:30 a.m.”，Julian 又確認 “half past nine”。9:30 a.m. = half past nine，所以兩種寫法都可。中伏位：不要只寫 “early”，因為 early 只是 Julian 的評價，不是時間。

3.explanation: 題目問 Audience，即對誰匯報。錄音說：“We’re presenting to all the department heads.”“presenting to” 對應 audience，所以答案是 all the department heads。department heads 是複數，因為前面有 all。

4.explanation: 題目問 Venue，即地點。錄音說：“The boardroom. You know, the big room on the top floor…”The boardroom 就是匯報地點。中伏位：“top floor with the view” 只是描述 boardroom，不是 venue 名稱。

5.explanation: 題目問 presentation 的 Length。錄音說三人各做 “5 PowerPoint slides each”，Bonnie 補充：“Which is 15 PowerPoint slides in total.”題目問整個 presentation 長度，所以要填 total：15 PowerPoint slides。中伏位：5 slides 是每人，不是總數。

6.explanation: 題目寫 “Bonnie: ___ of World Expos”。錄音說：“Bonnie is going to look at the history of World Expos.”“history of World Expos” 完全對應題目，所以填 history。history 是名詞，放在 “of World Expos” 前自然。

7.explanation: 題目寫 “Julian: ___ about World Expos”。錄音說：“You are looking at the good and bad things about World Expos.”所以 Julian 負責 good and bad things。中伏位：錄音也說 “bad things as well as the good”，意思相同，但答案最好用完整概念 good and bad things。

8.explanation: 題目寫 “Cherie: ___ of World Expos”。錄音說：“I’m looking at the future of World Expos.”“future of World Expos” 直接對應題目。future 是名詞，符合 “___ of World Expos”。

9.explanation: 題目在 work schedule 第一行問日期。錄音中 Cherie 先不確定是 8th 還是 9th，後來查電話，Julian 確認：“Wednesday the 9th of August.”中伏位：8th 是 Cherie 一開始不確定的日期，後面被修正為 9th，所以答案是 August 9。

10.answer: interview Mr Roy / interview Leo Roy’s dad
10.explanation: 題目問第一行要做什麼。錄音說 Leo 的爸爸曾在 Shanghai Expo 工作，Cherie說她 arranged to meet him “and interview him.”所以工作是 interview Mr Roy / Leo Roy’s father。注意：你貼出的表格 Person欄給了 J，但逐字稿說做這件事的是 Cherie；若原卷 Person 欄其實是 C，應以 Cherie 為準。

11.answer: attend a talk / go to a talk / a talk on Expos
11.explanation: 題目寫 “August 19 — B — ___ at Hong Kong Metropolitan University”。錄音說 Professor Leung 會在 Hong Kong Metropolitan University “giving a talk about World Expos”，Bonnie 說會記下 “A talk on Expos … on Saturday the 19th.”所以 Bonnie 要 attend/go to a talk。中伏位：不是 presentation；這是 Professor Leung 的 talk。

12.explanation: 題目問 Progress Meeting 的日期。Cherie 提議 Monday the 21st，但 Bonnie 說那天是 public holiday，然後提議 “the day after the public holiday”。August 21 後一天是 August 22，所以答案是 August 22。中伏位：21st 被否定，不能填。

13.explanation: 題目寫 “August 23 — ___ — Give Jasmine ___”。錄音中 Cherie 說：“I can give a first draft to Jasmine on the 23rd of August.”所以 person 是 Cherie / C。中伏位：Julian 只是重複記錄，不是執行者。

14.answer: the first draft of the PowerPoint presentation / first draft
14.explanation: 題目寫 “Give Jasmine ___”。錄音說：“I can give a first draft to Jasmine…” 前文亦說是 “first draft of the PowerPoint presentation”。所以答案是 first draft / first draft of the PowerPoint presentation。中伏位：不是 final version，只是 first draft。

15.explanation: 題目寫 “August 26 — ___ — ___”。錄音中 Cherie 說：“How about doing it on Saturday 26th? All of us will need to do it.”“All of us” 對應表格 Person 欄的 All。

16.explanation: 題目問 August 26 要做什麼。錄音說：“Could we practise the presentation sometime around about then? How about doing it on Saturday 26th?”所以答案是 practise the presentation。中伏位：不是正式 presentation，正式 presentation 是 August 30。

17.explanation: 題目寫 lecture topic：“A History of World Expos: ___”。錄音說：“the topic of my lecture tonight is ‘A History of World Expos: Bringing People Together’.”冒號後的副標題就是答案。中伏位：前面提到 Shanghai 2010，但那只是引入，不是 lecture title。

18.answer: decide on a theme / deciding on a theme
18.explanation: 題目問 host countries 的 roles。錄音說 host country has two major things to do，第一是：“Decide on a theme for the exhibition.”所以第一個 role 是 decide on a theme。theme 是 Expo 的 focus，這是補充，不是另一個 role。

19.answer: invite other countries to join the exhibition
19.explanation: 題目問第二個 host role。錄音說：“the host has to invite other countries to join the exhibition.”這句幾乎直接給答案。中伏位：不是 “join the country”，而是 join the exhibition。

20.explanation: 題目問 London Expo 的 number of visitors。錄音說：“6.3 million visitors came to see the Great Exhibition.”所以答案是 6.3 million。中伏位：Ten countries 是參展國數目，不是 visitors

21.answer: grew / growing the biggest flower in the world
21.explanation: 題目問 The Great Exhibition 的 major achievements。錄音說第一個 major achievement 是 “they grew the biggest flower in the world.”所以答案可以寫 grew the biggest flower in the world / growing the biggest flower in the world。中伏位：child could stand on its leaf 是用來形容花很大，不是 achievement 本身。

22.explanation: 題目問第二個 major achievement。錄音說：“The second major achievement was raising awareness of farming techniques.”這句直接對應答案。中伏位：錄音提到 industry and farming，但本題要的是 achievement，所以要寫 awareness of farming techniques。

23.explanation: 題目問 Stage 2 的名稱。錄音說：“The second stage … focused on Cultural Exchange. This stage is called ‘Cultural Exchange’…”所以答案是 Cultural Exchange。大小寫不影響理解，但正式答案可首字母大寫。

24.explanation: 題目問 Stage 2 的 period。錄音說：“from about 1939 to 1987.”所以答案是 1939–1987。中伏位：1939 也同時是 New York Expo 年份，但這裡整個 stage 的 period 是 1939–1987。

25.explanation: 題目問 New York Expo theme。錄音說：“the theme of this World Expo was‘The City of Tomorrow’.”所以答案是 The City of Tomorrow。中伏位：New York / America 是地點，不是 theme。

26.explanation: 題目問 examples of exhibits。錄音說 New York Expo had “huge exhibitions on modern food”。所以第一個例子是 modern food。modern 是形容詞，修飾 food。

27.answer: latest works of art / works of art / art
27.explanation: 題目問另一個 exhibit example。錄音說 New York Expo “displayed the latest works of art from different countries.”所以答案是 latest works of art / works of art。中伏位：food and art 是 cultural aspects；若空格較短，art 也可接受。

28.explanation: 題目問 number of countries which took part。錄音說：“50 countries took part.”所以答案是 50。中伏位：44 million 是 visitors，不是 countries。

29.explanation: 題目問 Nation Branding 的 period。錄音說：“started around 1988 and is still going on now.”所以答案是 1988–now / 1988–present。中伏位：Hanover 只是例子，不是 stage 開始時間。

30.explanation: 題目問 Hanover Expo theme。錄音說：“The theme for this Expo was ‘Nature and Technology’.”所以答案是 Nature and Technology。中伏位：environmentally-friendly products 是主題下的 idea，不是主題名稱。

31.answer: the number of visitors was lower than expected / only about 25 million people came
31.explanation: 你貼出的題目寫 “Reason why considered to be a success”，但逐字稿說：“the number of visitors was lower than what had been expected. Only about 25 million people came … so it was considered to be a bit of a failure.”所以按逐字稿，這題應該是問 failure 的原因，答案是 visitor numbers were lower than expected / only about 25 million came。若原題真的寫 success，逐字稿沒有提供 “success” 的原因，不能硬作答案。

32.answer: millions of dollars wasted / money could be better spent
32.explanation: 題目在 “Downsides of having an Expo” 下。錄音說第一個 downside 是 “the millions of dollars wasted on World Expos” and “the money could be better spent.”所以答案是 money wasted / millions of dollars wasted。中伏位：host country spends millions 是成本說明；題目要 downside，所以重點是 money wasted。

33.answer: disruption to life in the host city
33.explanation: 題目問另一個 downside。Julian 說：“One of the other downsides … is the disruption to life in the host city.”這句直接給答案。中伏位：roads improved / constructed 是造成 disruption 的原因，不是最完整答案。

34.answer: Expo buildings are not used again / buildings are not re-used
34.explanation: 題目問第三個 downside。Cherie 說 people complain that “the Expo buildings are not used again after the end of the Expo”，又補充 “more often than not they are just taken down.”所以答案是 buildings not reused / not used again。中伏位：occasionally re-used 是少數情況，真正 downside 是通常不重用。

35.answer: friendship among different countries / international friendship
35.explanation: 題目寫 “To promote ___”。Bonnie 說 first reason is “to promote friendship among different countries”，又說 “promote international friendship.”所以兩種寫法都可。中伏位：countries work together 是原因；要填的是 friendship。

36.explanation: 題目寫 “To attract ___”。Bonnie 說：“holding Expos can attract business and tourism.”所以答案是 business and tourism。中伏位：national image 是上一項已給例子，不是這格答案。

37.answer: less writing / take out some writing
37.explanation: 題目問 PowerPoint layout suggestions。Bonnie 說 slides are “a bit wordy” and“too many words on each slide”，Cherie 回應 “take out some of the writing.”wordy / too many words → less writing，所以答案是 less writing。中伏位：content light 是內容問題，不是 layout suggestion。

38.explanation: Julian 說：“we could put in more visuals, you know, more pictures.”more visuals = more pictures，所以答案是 more visuals / more pictures。visuals是名詞，指圖片或視覺元素。

39.answer: change the background colour to light blue / light blue background
39.explanation: Julian 建議：“change the background colour to light blue.” Cherie 亦確認：“change the background colour to light blue.”所以答案是 light blue background / change background to light blue。中伏位：white 是原本背景，不是建議答案。

40.explanation: Julian 說：“put all the main headings in red instead of having all the writing in black.” Cherie 記下：“put headings in red.”所以答案是 put headings in red。中伏位：black 是原本顏色，不是建議。

41.explanation: Julian 說 writing is “a bit small”，所以 “make it bigger so it’s easier for the audience to read.”small 是問題，bigger 是建議。答案是 make the writing bigger。

42.answer: change the font to make it look more modern / use a more modern font
42.explanation: Julian 說 Times New Roman looks old-fashioned，問可否 make it more“up-to-date” looking。Cherie 記下：“change the font to make it look more modern.”up-to-date = modern，所以答案是 change font / more modern font。中伏位：Times New Roman 是要避免的舊字體，不是答案。

43.answer: change numbers to bullet points / use bullet points
43.explanation: Cherie 問 numbers or bullet points，Bonnie 說 bullet points would look better，Cherie 記下：“change numbers to bullet points.”所以答案是 bullet points。中伏位：numbers 是原本用了的格式，不是最後建議。

44.answer: to let ordinary people see things from around the world
44.explanation: 題目問 ordinary people 眼中 World Expos 的 main function。Leo 說 main function “wasn’t trade or science” but “the only way that normal people could see things from around the world.”所以答案是讓普通人看到世界各地的東西。中伏位：trade / science 被明確排除。

45.explanation: 題目問有多少人被展出。Leo 說：“more than 35,000 men, women and children were exhibited…”所以答案是 more than 35,000。中伏位：end of 19th / into 20th century 是時間，不是人數。

46.explanation: 題目要 human zoos 中的人要做的 activities，例子已給 “lived in traditional houses”。錄音接着說：“they did the cooking and so on.”所以答案是 did the cooking / cooked。這是活動動作，符合題目 “had to do”

47.answer: put on exotic shows / did dances / performed religious rituals
47.explanation: 錄音說：“they put on some sort of exotic show — doing some dances or religious rituals.”所以可填 put on exotic shows / did dances / performed religious rituals。中伏位：people watched them like monkeys 是觀眾行為，不是被展出者的 activity

48.answer: because they were pygmies / because they were the smallest people in the world
48.explanation: 題目問 Ota Benga 和族人為什麼被 W.J. McGee 選中。錄音說 McGee wanted“the most extreme examples of man … the tallest, the smallest”，所以 he got“the smallest people from Africa”，即 Ota Benga 的 pygmy tribe。所以答案是因為他們是 pygmies，被視為世界上最矮小的人。中伏位：不是因為他們文化特別，而是因為 McGee 想展出 “extreme examples”。

49.answer: they were in the USA to show off their own culture
49.explanation: 題目問 pygmies 以為自己到美國的目的。錄音說：“Ota Benga and his fellow tribespeople thought that they were in the USA to show off their own culture.”所以答案是 show off their own culture。中伏位：這是他們以為的目的，不是 Expo 真正怎樣宣傳他們。

50.answer: they were advertised as the most primitive people on the planet
50.explanation: 題目問實際宣傳與他們想法的 contrast。錄音說 they were advertised “to the public and scientists as the most primitive people on the planet.”所以答案是 they were advertised as the most primitive people on the planet。中伏位：primitive 是 Expo 宣傳中的貶低說法，不是他們自己的自我介紹。

51.answer: a live exhibit / live exhibit in the zoo
51.explanation: 題目問 Ota Benga 在 New York zoo 的 job。錄音說他以為會 look after elephants, “but he was actually given a job to be a live exhibit in the zoo.”所以答案是 a live exhibit。中伏位：look after the elephants 是他以為的工作，不是實際工作。

52.answer: they protested and wrote to newspapers complaining about it
52.explanation: 題目問 New York people 的反應。Leo 說：“they did protest and write to the newspapers complaining about it.”所以答案是 protested and wrote to newspapers。中伏位：exhibition stopped after a week 是結果；題目問 reaction，所以重點是 protest / complaints。

53.answer: No — he was homesick and never returned to Africa
53.explanation: 題目問故事是否有 happy ending。錄音說事情 “got worse and worse”，Ota Benga homesick，想回 Africa，但 “didn’t have enough money”，所以 “he never returned to Africa.”所以不是 happy ending。中伏位：他有在 tobacco factory 工作，但那不是 happy ending 的原因；關鍵是他想回家卻回不了。

54.answer: Yes; because Jasmine wanted the full picture
54.explanation: 題目問 Bonnie 是否認為應放入 presentation。Bonnie 說：“I think we should.Jasmine wanted the full picture, so this gives them the full picture…”所以 Bonnie = Yes；原因是 gives the full picture of the history of these Expos。中伏位：她不是因為故事 shocking 才說要放，而是因為 Jasmine 要 full picture。

55.answer: No / not keen; because some audience members are American and they do not want to offend anyone
55.explanation: Cherie 說：“I’m not so keen”，原因是 “a couple of the audience … are actually American” and “we don’t want to offend anybody.”所以 Cherie = No / not keen；原因是怕冒犯美國觀眾。中伏位：她不是否認故事重要，而是擔心 presentation 場合和 audience reaction。

56.answer: Yes, but only the first half; because only the first half is directly relevant to Expos
56.explanation: Julian 說：“I think we should. But only the first half of his story is directly relevant to expos. His experiences in New York and the zoo are less relevant.”所以 Julian = Yes, partly / first half only；原因是保持 relevant。中伏位：他不是完全反對 New York zoo 部分的真實性，而是覺得那部分與 Expos 較不直接相關。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: OK, I know you’ve started doing some work for this World Expos presentation we have to do. So I just wanted to check where we are and maybe plan out the next few weeks.
1.zh: 好的，我知道你們已經開始為我們要做的世界博覽會簡報做一些準備工作了。所以我只是想確認一下目前進度，並且也許可以規劃接下來幾週的工作。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Yeah, I was thinking the same. Jasmine has—hold on. Hold on. What was it about again?
1.zh: 對，我也正有同樣的想法。Jasmine 已經——等等，等等。這簡報主題又是關於什麼的？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Right. Well, the title we were given was An overview of World Expos. Remember, Julian?
1.zh: 好吧。嗯，我們拿到的題目是《世界博覽會概覽》。Julian，你記得吧？

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Oh yeah, vaguely. So when is it? The presentation.
1.zh: 哦，對，有一點印象。那是什麼時候？我是說那個簡報。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Well, that’s what I was going to say. Jasmine’s now confirmed all the details. So we’re presenting on August 30th at 9:30 a.m.
1.zh: 嗯，這正是我剛想說的。Jasmine 現在已經確認了所有細節。我們會在 8 月 30 日上午 9 時 30 分進行簡報。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: OK. Right… August 30th at half past nine. That’s early then! Wait, is that all three of us presenting?
1.zh: 好的。8 月 30 日，九點半。那可真早！等等，是我們三個人都要簡報嗎？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Yeah, that’s what we agreed on.
1.zh: 是的，這是我們之前說好的。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: OK, just checking. And who are we presenting to?
1.zh: 好的，我只是確認一下。那我們是向誰簡報？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Do you never pay attention? We’re presenting to all the department heads.
1.zh: 你是不是從來都沒有專心聽？我們是向所有部門主管簡報。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: All the department heads! Wow, no pressure there then! And where are we presenting?
1.zh: 所有部門主管！哇，那壓力可不小啊！我們在哪裡簡報？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: The boardroom. You know, the big room on the top floor with the view and…
1.zh: 在董事會會議室。你知道的，就是頂樓那間很大的房間，可以看到景色，還有……

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Yeah, yeah, I know where the boardroom is. Well, we’d better get going then. How much do we need to get ready? I mean, how long does it have to be?
1.zh: 知道，知道，我知道董事會會議室在哪裡。那我們最好開始準備了。我們需要準備多少內容？我的意思是，簡報要多長？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Well, all three of us will be doing a section. So I think if we do 5 PowerPoint slides each.
1.zh: 嗯，我們三個人每人會負責一個部分。所以我想，如果我們每人做 5 張 PowerPoint 投影片。

1.speaker: Bonnie
1.text: Yeah, that’s what I was thinking. 5 slides each. Which is 15 PowerPoint slides in total.
1.zh: 對，我也是這樣想的。每人 5 張投影片。也就是總共 15 張 PowerPoint 投影片。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: So, just to confirm, what were the three sections again?
1.zh: 所以，我再確認一下，三個部分分別是什麼？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: You are joking, aren’t you? (pause) Right, I can see you’re not. Right, well Bonnie is going to look at the history of World Expos.
1.zh: 你是在開玩笑，對吧？（停頓）好吧，我看得出來你不是。好，Bonnie 會負責研究世界博覽會的歷史。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Oh, I thought you were doing the history of World Expos!
1.zh: 哦，我以為是你負責世界博覽會的歷史！

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: No, that’s Bonnie doing that. You are looking at the good and bad things about World Expos.
1.zh: 不是，那是 Bonnie 負責的。你負責研究世界博覽會的好處和壞處。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Yeah, yeah, I remember Jasmine did say she wanted us to find the bad things as well as the good. So, what are you doing, Cherie?
1.zh: 對，對，我記得 Jasmine 確實說過，她希望我們找出壞處，也要找出好處。那 Cherie，你負責什麼？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: I’m looking at the future of World Expos, remember? We already read a bit on the future of World Expos online on the webpage.
1.zh: 我負責研究世界博覽會的未來，記得嗎？我們已經在網頁上讀過一些關於世界博覽會未來的資料。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Oh, yeah, OK. I remember.
1.zh: 哦，對，好的。我想起來了。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Right, so what I wanted to do today was to draw up a work schedule. You know, so we know who’s doing what and when.
1.zh: 好，所以我今天想做的是擬定一份工作時間表。也就是讓我們知道誰負責什麼，以及什麼時候完成。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: OK, maybe I can take notes and send you it later.
1.zh: 好的，也許我可以做筆記，稍後再發給你們。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Oh, I was going to say, I was speaking to a friend of mine, Leo Roy, the other day. You know Leo?
1.zh: 哦，我正想說，前幾天我和我的一個朋友 Leo Roy 聊過。你認識 Leo 嗎？

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: No, no.
1.zh: 不，不認識。

1.speaker: Bonnie
1.text: Yeah, I know Leo, remember?
1.zh: 我認識 Leo，記得嗎？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Oh, yeah, of course (laughs). Well, Leo told me his dad worked on the Shanghai Expo in 2010, so I’ve arranged to meet up with him—his dad, I mean—and interview him.
1.zh: 哦，對，當然記得（笑）。Leo告訴我，他爸爸曾參與 2010 年上海世博會的工作，所以我已經安排和他見面——我是說和他爸爸見面——並訪問他。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Fantastic—so when are you meeting him?
1.zh: 太好了——那你什麼時候和他見面？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Oh, I can’t remember. It was either the 8th or 9th of August. Something like that.
1.zh: 哦，我不太記得了。應該是 8 月 8 日或 9 日。差不多是那個時候。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: So, which was it? We’re trying to do a schedule here.
1.zh: 所以到底是哪一天？我們現在是在排時間表。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Right, let me check my phone. (Pause). Right, the Wednesday.
1.zh: 好，讓我看一下手機。（停頓）好，是星期三。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Hold on. So you’re interviewing Mr. Roy on Wednesday the 9th of August. Is his surname spelled R-O-Y?
1.zh: 等等。所以你是在 8 月 9 日星期三訪問 Roy 先生。他的姓氏是拼作 R-O-Y 嗎？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Yes it is!
1.zh: 是的！

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: You were pretty sure about that! (Laughs).
1.zh: 這點你倒是很肯定！（笑）

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Hey, did you read the email from Jasmine? She said that a Professor Leung at the Hong Kong Metropolitan University is giving a talk about World Expos. One of us should go.
1.zh: 嘿，你們有看 Jasmine 的電郵嗎？她說香港都會大學的 Leung教授會舉辦一場關於世界博覽會的講座。我們其中一個人應該去聽。

1.speaker: Bonnie
1.text: Mm… Do you know when that is?
1.zh: 嗯……你知道是什麼時候嗎？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: I think she said Saturday morning on 19th August. I can’t go to it. Bonnie, why don’t you go? You could see if we can include some of the information in our presentation on the 30th.
1.zh: 我想她說是 8 月 19 日星期六早上。我不能去。Bonnie，不如你去吧？你可以看看我們能否把其中一些資料放進 30 日的簡報裡。

1.speaker: Bonnie
1.text: Yeah, great! OK, I’ll make a note of that. A talk on Expos at the Metropolitan University, on Saturday the 19th.
1.zh: 好啊，太好了！好的，我會記下來。19 日星期六，在都會大學有一場關於博覽會的講座。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Great. So, I think we should meet up at some point to talk about all the information we’ve collected.
1.zh: 很好。所以我覺得我們應該找個時間見面，討論一下我們收集到的所有資料。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Good idea. When’d be a good time for you?
1.zh: 好主意。你什麼時候方便？

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: How about Monday the 21st?
1.zh: 21 日星期一怎麼樣？

1.speaker: Bonnie
1.text: No, it’s a public holiday, remember? How about the day after the public holiday then?
1.zh: 不行，那天是公眾假期，記得嗎？那公眾假期之後一天怎麼樣？

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: For what? Sorry, I was miles away.
1.zh: 做什麼？抱歉，我剛才走神了。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: For the progress meeting.
1.zh: 開進度會議。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Yeah, fine, yeah.
1.zh: 可以，可以。

1.speaker: Bonnie
1.text: Yeah, me too. OK, well, then I’m happy to take all the information and do a first draft of the PowerPoint presentation if you like.
1.zh: 我也可以。好的，那如果你們願意，我可以把所有資料整理起來，做出 PowerPoint 簡報的初稿。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Fantastic—thanks, Cherie. When do you think you can get the first draft of the PowerPoint presentation done by? Jasmine said she’d definitely have to see it beforehand.
1.zh: 太好了——謝謝你，Cherie。你覺得你什麼時候可以完成 PowerPoint 簡報初稿？Jasmine 說她一定要事先看過。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: I can give a first draft to Jasmine on the 23rd of August. It will take me a few hours to put it all together.
1.zh: 我可以在 8 月 23 日把初稿交給 Jasmine。把所有內容整理起來大概會花我幾個小時。

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: OK. Give Jasmine the first draft of the PowerPoint presentation on the 23rd of August.
1.zh: 好的。8 月 23 日把 PowerPoint 簡報初稿交給 Jasmine。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Great. Could we practise the presentation sometime around about then? How about doing it on Saturday 26th? All of us will need to do it. Would that be okay?
1.zh: 很好。那我們能不能在那前後找個時間練習簡報？8 月 26 日星期六怎麼樣？我們所有人都需要參與。可以嗎？

1.speaker: Bonnie
1.text: Yeah, that’s fine with me.
1.zh: 可以，我沒問題。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Fantastic. Is that fine with you, Julian?
1.zh: 太好了。Julian，你也可以嗎？

1.speaker: Julian
1.text: Sure. No problem.
1.zh: 當然，沒問題。

1.speaker: Cherie
1.text: Great—looks like we are very organised.
1.zh: 很好——看來我們安排得很有條理。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining me here this evening.
2.zh: 各位女士、先生，晚上好。感謝大家今晚蒞臨參加。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: In 2010, Shanghai celebrated the biggest ever World Expo. Millions of people from all over the world came to Shanghai to see the exhibits and innovations the Expo had to offer.
2.zh: 2010 年，上海舉辦了歷來規模最大的世界博覽會。來自世界各地的數百萬人來到上海，參觀世博會展示的展品和創新成果。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: It is this coming together of people that makes World Expos so special to me.
2.zh: 正是這種人們聚集在一起的情景，使世界博覽會在我心目中特別有意義。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: And that’s why the topic of my lecture tonight is “A History of World Expos: Bringing People Together”, because Expos do just that—they bring people together.
2.zh: 也正因如此，我今晚講座的題目是《世界博覽會的歷史：凝聚人群》，因為博覽會正是這樣做的——它們把人們聚集在一起。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: So first, I thought I’d tell you a little bit about what Expos are and then we’ll explore the history of World Expos, which I shall break into three stages to show you how they developed into the World Expos we know today.
2.zh: 所以，首先我會先簡單介紹博覽會是什麼，然後我們會探討世界博覽會的歷史。我會把這段歷史分為三個階段，向大家說明它們是如何發展成今日我們所認識的世界博覽會。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: What are World Expos?
2.zh: 什麼是世界博覽會？

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: World Expos are, quite simply, international exhibitions.
2.zh: 簡單來說，世界博覽會就是國際展覽。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: One country is the host.
2.zh: 其中一個國家會擔任主辦國。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Basically, the host country has two major things to do:
2.zh: 基本上，主辦國有兩項主要工作：

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Decide on a theme for the exhibition.
2.zh: 第一，決定展覽的主題。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The theme is very important for the Expo as it gives it its focus.
2.zh: 主題對博覽會非常重要，因為它為博覽會提供焦點。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Having decided on a theme, the host has to invite other countries to join the exhibition.
2.zh: 在決定主題之後，主辦國必須邀請其他國家參與展覽。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: History of World Expos – Three Stages
2.zh: 世界博覽會的歷史——三個階段

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The first phase or stage is focused on industrial and technological inventions.
2.zh: 第一個階段聚焦於工業和科技發明。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: This phase began way back in 1851 and really lasted until about 1938.
2.zh: 這個階段早在 1851 年開始，並一直持續到大約 1938 年。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: So the very first World Expo was held in 1851, in the wonderful city of London, England.
2.zh: 第一屆世界博覽會於 1851 年在英國美麗的城市倫敦舉行。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: It was called “The Great Exhibition”, and the idea was to promote all the very latest inventions for improving industry and farming.
2.zh: 它名為「萬國工業博覽會」，其理念是推廣所有能改善工業和農業的最新發明。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Ten countries, including China, were invited to join in and display their latest technology.
2.zh: 包括中國在內的十個國家受邀參與，並展示它們的最新科技。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: 6.3 million visitors came to see the Great Exhibition.
2.zh: 共有 630 萬名參觀者前來參觀這場萬國工業博覽會。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: It was a truly amazing event.
2.zh: 這確實是一場令人驚嘆的盛事。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The Great Exhibition had several major achievements, but I’d like to highlight two:
2.zh: 這場萬國工業博覽會有幾項重大成就，但我想重點介紹其中兩項：

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The first is what people thought was the major achievement of the Great Exhibition at the time, which was they grew the biggest flower in the world.
2.zh: 第一項是當時人們認為這場博覽會最重大的成就，那就是他們培育出了世界上最大的花。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: And this flower was so big a child could stand on its leaf.
2.zh: 這朵花大得足以讓一個小孩站在它的葉子上。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The second major achievement was raising awareness of farming techniques.
2.zh: 第二項重大成就是提高了人們對農業技術的認識。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The increase of awareness of different farming techniques learnt from the Great Expo brought huge benefits to the world.
2.zh: 從這場博覽會學到的不同農業技術，使人們的認識提高，並為世界帶來巨大益處。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The second stage in the development of World Expos focused on Cultural Exchange.
2.zh: 世界博覽會發展的第二個階段聚焦於文化交流。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: This stage is called “Cultural Exchange” because from about 1939 to 1987, World Expos focused more on themes that were important culturally.
2.zh: 這個階段稱為「文化交流」，因為從大約 1939 年到 1987 年，世界博覽會更注重具有文化意義的主題。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: One of the first World Expos of this kind took place in New York, America, in 1939.
2.zh: 這類世界博覽會的早期例子之一，是 1939 年在美國紐約舉行的博覽會。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: As I have said before, all World Expos have a particular theme, and the theme of this World Expo was “The City of Tomorrow”.
2.zh: 正如我之前所說，所有世界博覽會都有一個特定主題，而這屆世界博覽會的主題是「明日之城」。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: To show the city of tomorrow, the New York Expo had huge exhibitions on modern food and displayed the latest works of art from different countries.
2.zh: 為了展示明日之城，紐約世博會舉辦了大型現代食品展覽，並展出來自不同國家的最新藝術作品。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: So it combined different aspects of culture: food and art.
2.zh: 因此，它結合了文化的不同面向：食物和藝術。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Again, this was a very popular World Expo.
2.zh: 同樣地，這是一屆非常受歡迎的世界博覽會。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: 50 countries took part and over 44 million people went to it.
2.zh: 共有 50 個國家參與，超過 4,400萬人前往參觀。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Finally, the third stage in the development of World Expos was really all about Nation Branding.
2.zh: 最後，世界博覽會發展的第三個階段主要關乎國家品牌塑造。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The Nation Branding stage started around 1988 and is still going on now, really.
2.zh: 國家品牌塑造階段大約始於 1988 年，實際上至今仍在持續。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: This meant that the host country and all participating countries used the Expo to promote themselves.
2.zh: 這意味著主辦國和所有參展國都利用博覽會來宣傳自己。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: An example of an Expo in the Nation Branding stage took place in Hanover, Germany.
2.zh: 國家品牌塑造階段的一個例子，是在德國漢諾威舉行的博覽會。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The theme for this Expo was “Nature and Technology”.
2.zh: 這屆博覽會的主題是「自然與科技」。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: The idea was to promote environmentally-friendly products and inventions and to look at ways of saving the environment.
2.zh: 其理念是推廣環保產品和發明，並探索保護環境的方法。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: 155 countries were invited, but unfortunately the number of visitors was lower than what had been expected.
2.zh: 共有 155 個國家受邀參與，但遺憾的是，參觀人數低於預期。

2.speaker: Professor Leung
2.text: Only about 25 million people came to the Expo, so it was considered to be a bit of a failure.
2.zh: 只有大約 2,500 萬人前來參觀，因此它被認為有點失敗。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: OK, so what do you think?
3.zh: 好了，你們覺得怎麼樣？

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Well, I think it’s brilliant overall. You’ve done a really good job.
3.zh: 嗯，整體來說我覺得很出色。你做得非常好。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: But… I’m sensing a “but” here! (laughs)
3.zh: 但是……我感覺這裡有一個「但是」！（笑）

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: (laughs) Well, I think it might be a bit light on content.
3.zh: （笑）嗯，我覺得內容可能有點不足。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: OK, so I was thinking that as well. We could maybe add a couple more slides. What do you think is missing or could be expanded on?
3.zh: 好的，其實我也有這樣想。我們也許可以再加幾張投影片。你覺得缺少了什麼，或者有哪些地方可以再擴充？

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Yeah, I was wondering if we needed more on the downsides, you know, negatives about organising World Expos. So, I would add a slide on that.
3.zh: 對，我在想我們是否需要多講一些負面方面，也就是舉辦世界博覽會的壞處。所以我會加一張關於這方面的投影片。

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Maybe include some key points on the slide. The first one would be something about the millions of dollars wasted on World Expos, and the fact that the money could be better spent.
3.zh: 也許可以在投影片上加入一些重點。第一點可以是關於世界博覽會浪費數百萬美元，以及這些錢本可以用在更好的地方。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: Yeah, I’d include something like that. I mean, the host country has to be prepared to spend millions on creating a World Expo.
3.zh: 對，我也會加入類似的內容。我的意思是，主辦國必須準備花費數百萬美元來舉辦世界博覽會。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: One of the other downsides we could include is the disruption to life in the host city.
3.zh: 我們可以加入的另一個壞處，是對主辦城市居民生活造成的干擾。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: You know, World Expos have to be built and existing roads to the Expo site have to be improved or new roads have to be constructed.
3.zh: 你知道，世界博覽會場地必須興建，而且通往會場的現有道路必須改善，或者需要興建新道路。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: So, it can cause a lot of disruption for people living in the host city.
3.zh: 因此，這可能會對主辦城市居民的生活造成很大干擾。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Another disadvantage we could include is that very often people complain that the Expo buildings are not used again after the end of the Expo.
3.zh: 我們可以加入的另一個缺點是，人們經常抱怨博覽會結束後，那些博覽會建築不會再被使用。

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Really?
3.zh: 真的嗎？

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Yeah, occasionally the buildings are re-used, but more often than not they are just taken down so, no, they’re not re-used.
3.zh: 是的，偶爾那些建築會被重新使用，但更多時候它們只是被拆除，所以，沒錯，它們通常不會被重用。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: OK, well I think I can do a slide on that. Is there anything else to include? Another slide maybe?
3.zh: 好的，我覺得我可以就這一點做一張投影片。還有其他需要加入的內容嗎？也許再加一張投影片？

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Well, I think we could include one on the reasons why a city would want to host a World Expo. I don’t think that comes across in our slides.
3.zh: 嗯，我覺得我們可以加入一張關於為什麼一個城市會想舉辦世界博覽會的投影片。我覺得我們目前的投影片沒有清楚呈現這一點。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: So, what would you include then, Bonnie? What kind of reasons?
3.zh: 那你會加入什麼內容呢，Bonnie？哪些理由？

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Well, there are lots of reasons. The first reason for holding a World Expo would be to promote friendship among different countries.
3.zh: 嗯，理由有很多。舉辦世界博覽會的第一個原因，是促進不同國家之間的友誼。

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Many different countries work together on each Expo, so it’s a wonderful way to promote international friendship.
3.zh: 許多不同國家會在每一屆博覽會中合作，所以這是促進國際友誼的絕佳方式。

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: The second reason for holding World Expos is so that different countries that take part in World Expos can build up their national image.
3.zh: 舉辦世界博覽會的第二個原因，是讓參與世界博覽會的不同國家可以建立自己的國家形象。

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: You know, countries can show how beautiful their countries are and how friendly their people are.
3.zh: 你知道，各國可以展示自己的國家有多美麗，以及人民有多友善。

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Plus, holding Expos can attract business and tourism.
3.zh: 此外，舉辦博覽會可以吸引商業活動和旅遊業。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Right, OK. Got it. I’ll include all these points in two extra slides. I’ll get the draft ready to give to Jasmine. Thanks guys.
3.zh: 好，明白了。我會把這些重點放進兩張額外的投影片裡。我會準備好初稿交給 Jasmine。謝謝你們。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Any comments on the presentation, I mean the way it looks and—
3.zh: 關於簡報還有什麼意見嗎？我是指它的外觀和——

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Well, I think generally it’s a bit wordy. You know too many words on each slide.
3.zh: 嗯，我覺得整體來說文字有點多。你知道，每張投影片上的字太多了。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: So, could we take out some of the writing?
3.zh: 所以，我們可以刪掉一些文字嗎？

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: OK, less writing, right. Hang on, let me get my laptop to write these comments down so I don’t forget. (Pause). OK.
3.zh: 好的，減少文字，對吧。等一下，讓我拿出筆記型電腦把這些意見記下來，免得忘記。（停頓）好了。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: That would help definitely. Plus I was thinking we could put in more visuals, you know, more pictures.
3.zh: 那肯定會有幫助。另外，我在想我們可以加入更多視覺元素，也就是更多圖片。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: I think it would make the presentation look much more interesting. What do you think?
3.zh: 我覺得這會讓簡報看起來更有趣。你覺得呢？

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Sure. I can add more visuals.
3.zh: 當然。我可以加入更多視覺元素。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: Yeah, another point I thought of was to change the background colour to light blue.
3.zh: 對，我想到的另一點是把背景顏色改成淺藍色。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: White looks a bit boring, so why not have a light blue background instead of white, so it looks more colourful?
3.zh: 白色看起來有點沉悶，所以為什麼不用淺藍色背景取代白色，讓它看起來更有色彩？

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Yeah, I had a similar comment I’d noted down. What do you think, Cherie?
3.zh: 對，我也記下了類似的意見。Cherie，你覺得呢？

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Yep, fine. I was actually going to do that anyway in the next draft.
3.zh: 可以，沒問題。其實我本來也打算在下一版初稿中這樣做。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Okay, so change the background colour to light blue. What else?
3.zh: 好，所以把背景顏色改成淺藍色。還有什麼？

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: Another point is maybe put all the main headings in red instead of having all the writing in black just to make it look more interesting.
3.zh: 另一點是，也許可以把所有主要標題改成紅色，而不是所有文字都用黑色，這樣可以讓它看起來更有趣。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Yeah, good idea. So “put headings in red”.
3.zh: 對，好主意。所以是「把標題改成紅色」。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: Another point is the size of the writing. I think it’s a bit small—can we make it bigger so it’s easier for the audience to read?
3.zh: 還有一點是文字大小。我覺得字有點小——我們可以把它放大一點，讓觀眾更容易閱讀嗎？

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Mmm, so “make the writing bigger”.
3.zh: 嗯，所以是「把文字放大」。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: How about changing the font too? I always think Times New Roman looks so old-fashioned.
3.zh: 那也改一下字體怎麼樣？我一直覺得 Times New Roman看起來很過時。

3.speaker: Julian
3.text: Can we make it more, you know, “up-to-date” looking?
3.zh: 我們可以讓它看起來更，你知道，更「現代」一點嗎？

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Okay, change the font to make it look more modern.
3.zh: 好的，改變字體，讓它看起來更現代。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Actually, in relation to that—I was wondering whether we should use numbers or bullet points.
3.zh: 其實，說到這一點，我在想我們應該使用編號還是項目符號。

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: In the end, I used numbers, but do you think bullet points would look better?
3.zh: 最後我用了編號，但你們覺得項目符號會不會看起來更好？

3.speaker: Bonnie
3.text: Yeah I do—less formal and more visual—
3.zh: 對，我覺得會——比較不正式，也更有視覺效果——

3.speaker: Cherie
3.text: Okay, so change numbers to bullet points. Right, OK. Got it. I’ll get the draft ready to give to Jasmine then. Thanks guys.
3.zh: 好的，所以把編號改成項目符號。好，明白了。那我會準備好初稿交給 Jasmine。謝謝你們。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: OK, right, I’ve got my cappuccino. Anybody else want anything?
4.zh: 好了，我拿到我的卡布奇諾了。還有誰想要什麼嗎？

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: No thanks.
4.zh: 不用了，謝謝。

4.speaker: Cherie
4.text: No, no.
4.zh: 不用，不用。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: No, thanks Leo. How you doing anyway?
4.zh: 不用了，謝謝 Leo。你最近怎麼樣？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: I’m OK.
4.zh: 我還好。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: Good.
4.zh: 那就好。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Right, well, I remembered you said to look out for some stuff about Expos, so I asked my dad and he sent me a link on YouTube.
4.zh: 好，嗯，我記得你們說過要我留意一些關於博覽會的資料，所以我問了我爸爸，他傳給我一個 YouTube 連結。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: I thought it might be quite interesting for you.
4.zh: 我覺得這對你們來說可能挺有意思。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: You did say you were looking into the negative aspects of World Expos and trade fairs, so this you might call the dark side of the history.
4.zh: 你們確實說過正在研究世界博覽會和商展的負面方面，所以這可以說是歷史中黑暗的一面。

4.speaker: Cherie
4.text: Really?
4.zh: 真的嗎？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Yeah, the clip was basically about the experiences of this one African man called Ota Benga.
4.zh: 是的，那段影片主要是關於一名叫 Ota Benga 的非洲男子的經歷。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: The clip started off giving a pretty interesting insight into these World Exhibitions.
4.zh: 影片一開始對這些世界展覽提出了一個相當有趣的觀點。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: They said the main function of these expos for ordinary people wasn’t trade or science but rather it was the only way that normal people could see things from around the world.
4.zh: 影片說，這些博覽會對普通人而言，主要功能並不是貿易或科學，而是普通人能看到世界各地事物的唯一方式。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Very few people could travel abroad in those days, of course.
4.zh: 當然，在那個年代，能出國旅行的人非常少。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: Yeah, I’d never thought of that.
4.zh: 對，我從來沒有那樣想過。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Yeah, so that was one thing.
4.zh: 是的，這是一方面。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: But there was also this other more sinister, darker side of the Expos and fairs where they exhibited humans from different parts of the world, like in a human zoo.
4.zh: 但博覽會和商展還有另一個更陰暗、更可怕的一面，就是它們會展示來自世界不同地方的人，就像人類動物園一樣。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: They reckon that more than 35,000 men, women and children were exhibited in these types of human zoos at various Expos in Paris, London, the USA… at the end of the 19th and into the 20th Century.
4.zh: 據估計，在 19 世紀末到 20 世紀初，超過 35,000 名男女和兒童曾在巴黎、倫敦、美國等地各種博覽會中的這類人類動物園裡被展出。

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: Really? What did they make these people do in these human zoos?
4.zh: 真的嗎？他們讓這些人在那些人類動物園裡做什麼？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Well, once there, they had to live in traditional houses.
4.zh: 嗯，他們到那裡之後，必須住在傳統房屋裡。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: These traditional houses were built especially there.
4.zh: 這些傳統房屋是特地在那裡建造的。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: And these people, they did the cooking and so on.
4.zh: 而這些人會做飯等等。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: And people watched them like they watch monkeys at a zoo.
4.zh: 人們觀看他們，就像在動物園裡看猴子一樣。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: And at certain times of the day, they put on some sort of exotic show—doing some dances or religious rituals, that sort of thing.
4.zh: 在一天中的某些時段，他們還要表演某種異國風情的節目——例如跳舞或進行宗教儀式之類的活動。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: Wow, so it was really like the dolphin show at Ocean Park, then.
4.zh: 哇，那真的就像海洋公園的海豚表演一樣。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Yeah, pretty much.
4.zh: 對，差不多就是那樣。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: The most famous of these people who was in one of these human zoos was an African man named Ota Benga.
4.zh: 在這些人類動物園中，最有名的人之一是一名叫 Ota Benga的非洲男子。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: He was a pygmy.
4.zh: 他是俾格米人。

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: A what?
4.zh: 什麼人？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: A pygmy, you know, a tribe from Western Africa who were smaller than average humans.
4.zh: 俾格米人，你知道的，就是來自西非的一個部族，他們的身形比一般人矮小。

4.speaker: Cherie
4.text: Oh yeah, right.
4.zh: 哦，對，明白了。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: And that was the point. That’s why he was there.
4.zh: 而這正是重點。那就是他被帶到那裡的原因。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: What? Because he was a pygmy?
4.zh: 什麼？因為他是俾格米人？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Yeah. You see, for the 1904 Great World Fair in St Louis in the USA, there was this American scientist called W.J. McGee.
4.zh: 對。你看，在 1904 年美國聖路易舉行的世界博覽會上，有一位名叫 W.J. McGee 的美國科學家。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Now, McGee wanted to put on a spectacular exhibition of humankind.
4.zh: McGee 想舉辦一場壯觀的人類展覽。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: He wanted to exhibit the most extreme examples of man from around the world: the tallest, the smallest. That sort of thing.
4.zh: 他想展出來自世界各地最極端的人類例子：最高的人、最矮的人，諸如此類。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: So he got the smallest people from Africa.
4.zh: 所以他找來了非洲最矮小的人。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: And that was Ota Benga.
4.zh: 那就是 Ota Benga。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: He was from the tribe of pygmies—the smallest people in the world.
4.zh: 他來自俾格米部族——被視為世界上最矮小的人群。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: So, McGee sent this explorer on a huge expedition to Africa to find pygmies and bring them back.
4.zh: 因此，McGee 派了一名探險家前往非洲進行大規模遠征，尋找俾格米人並把他們帶回來。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: So, he did. He brought back Ota Benga and five other pygmies.
4.zh: 於是，那名探險家照做了。他帶回了 Ota Benga 和另外五名俾格米人。

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: Wow.
4.zh: 哇。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: That’s amazing.
4.zh: 真令人驚訝。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Yeah, I know.
4.zh: 對，我知道。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: The irony was that Ota Benga and his fellow tribespeople thought that they were in the USA to show off their own culture, whereas, in fact, what they were advertised to the public and scientists as was the most primitive people on the planet.
4.zh: 諷刺的是，Ota Benga 和他的族人以為他們到美國是為了展示自己的文化；然而事實上，他們被宣傳給公眾和科學家的形象，卻是地球上最原始的人。

4.speaker: Cherie
4.text: That’s terrible.
4.zh: 這太可怕了。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: And what happened after the fair ended?
4.zh: 那博覽會結束後發生了什麼？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Well, after the end of the fair, Ota went to New York.
4.zh: 嗯，博覽會結束後，Ota去了紐約。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: You imagine this little African guy in New York? You know, with all its skyscrapers and hi-tech lifestyle.
4.zh: 你能想像這個身材矮小的非洲男子在紐約嗎？你知道，那裡有那麼多摩天大樓和高科技生活方式。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: So, what did he do in New York? Did he work or?
4.zh: 那他在紐約做什麼？他有工作嗎，還是？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Well, sort of. He then became famous because he got a job at a zoo in New York.
4.zh: 嗯，算是有吧。後來他因為在紐約一家動物園找到一份工作而變得有名。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: He thought he was going to look after the elephants, but he was actually given a job to be a live exhibit in the zoo.
4.zh: 他以為自己會去照顧大象，但事實上，他得到的工作是在動物園裡當一個活體展品。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: He shared a cage with a chimpanzee.
4.zh: 他和一隻黑猩猩共用一個籠子。

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: That’s awful.
4.zh: 這太糟糕了。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Well, to be fair to people in New York, they did protest and write to the newspapers complaining about it.
4.zh: 嗯，公平地說，紐約人確實有抗議，也有寫信給報紙投訴這件事。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: So, what happened?
4.zh: 那後來怎樣？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: The exhibition was stopped after about a week.
4.zh: 那個展覽大約一週後就被停止了。

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: Good. So, then what happened to him?
4.zh: 太好了。那他之後怎樣？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: Well, it just got worse and worse for Ota.
4.zh: 嗯，對 Ota 來說，情況只是變得越來越糟。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: He then tried to settle in America and even ended up working in a tobacco factory, in a small town in the US.
4.zh: 後來他嘗試在美國定居，甚至最後在美國一個小鎮的煙草工廠工作。

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: But he was so homesick that he wanted to return to Africa but he didn’t have enough money to pay for the journey, so in the end he never returned to Africa.
4.zh: 但他非常思鄉，想回到非洲，卻沒有足夠的錢支付旅費，所以最後他再也沒有回到非洲。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: That’s terrible. No wonder it’s not very well known.
4.zh: 這太可悲了。難怪這件事不太為人所知。

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: That is a truly horrendous story, Leo.
4.zh: Leo，這真是一個極其可怕的故事。

4.speaker: Cherie
4.text: God, how can you treat somebody like that?
4.zh: 天啊，怎麼可以那樣對待一個人？

4.speaker: Leo
4.text: So, are you going to include it in the presentation?
4.zh: 那你們會把這件事放進簡報裡嗎？

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: What do you think, Bonnie?
4.zh: Bonnie，你覺得呢？

4.speaker: Bonnie
4.text: I think we should. Jasmine wanted the full picture, so this gives them the full picture of the history of these types of Expos, that’s for sure.
4.zh: 我覺得應該放。Jasmine 想要完整的圖像，而這肯定能讓他們更全面了解這類博覽會的歷史。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: Mm. Cherie?
4.zh: 嗯。Cherie 呢？

4.speaker: Cherie
4.text: Well, I’m not so keen. I mean, you have to remember that a couple of the audience when we present are actually American, from the USA.
4.zh: 嗯，我不是很贊成。我的意思是，你們要記得，我們簡報時有幾位觀眾其實是美國人，來自美國。

4.speaker: Cherie
4.text: I mean, we don’t want to offend anybody with our presentation, do we? What do you think, Julian?
4.zh: 我的意思是，我們不想因為簡報而冒犯任何人，對吧？Julian，你覺得呢？

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: Well, I think we should. But only the first half of his story is directly relevant to expos.
4.zh: 嗯，我覺得應該放。不過，他故事的前半部分才和博覽會有直接關係。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: His experiences in New York and the zoo are less relevant.
4.zh: 他在紐約和動物園的經歷就沒有那麼相關。

4.speaker: Julian
4.text: So, just including the first half would keep it relevant.
4.zh: 所以，只放前半部分可以讓內容保持相關。
